runners_data.name: High Calibre
runners_data.comment: Backward on debut when well beaten at Brighton 31 days ago after looking market fancied, High Calibre is bred to be most effective over further than today's 6f; sixth in our rankings, the question is whether he has progressed enough to trouble the leaders.

runners_data.name: Midgham Man
runners_data.comment: An unraced Study Of Man gelding whose dam performed well at 6f, Midgham Man is a half-brother to Be An Angel and has the right pedigree credentials for this trip; with a trainer capable of landing debuts and the market worth monitoring, he could make a bold introduction.

runners_data.name: Percy Shaw
runners_data.comment: Interference at Newbury on debut 18 days ago — beaten 8 lengths in what was a stronger contest than today's — means the form book can be treated with some caution; a shorter trip should suit his speed pedigree, though he is lightly raced and fifth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rogue Imperial
runners_data.comment: Stepped forward from debut to finish 4 lengths adrift in third in a novice at Lingfield 28 days ago, with that effort looking strong on ground and trip he handles; our highest-rated runner in the field, he is expected to go well and takes plenty of beating.

runners_data.name: Sea Palace
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 8¼ lengths on debut at Hamilton 19 days ago in a race where the form has been given a boost since; he showed he knew his job and should progress with that experience, and is effective at 6f on good to soft ground.

runners_data.name: Soldier Of The Sea
runners_data.comment: An unraced debutant with a January birthday making him among the more mature in the field, Soldier Of The Sea cost 100,000 euros at the breeze-up sales and is bred to be precocious; the market will be the best guide, though he is ranked last on our figures.

runners_data.name: This Moment
runners_data.comment: Eager in the preliminaries and drawn wide at Chester last time, This Moment went too hard early on a tight circuit and finished fourth beaten 4 lengths; a more conventional track here with a trainer in fine form gives him better conditions, and he is effective at 6f on good ground.

races.name: Dandara Golwg Gwendraeth Handicap

runners_data.name: Outer Edge
runners_data.note: Has winning similar-going form but is a natural hold-up operator forced into a compromised position given the volume of backmarkers in this field; Gina Mangan will need to find space from further back than ideal, and a 37-day break adds mild doubt over peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: A consistent placer in recent starts yet to score, Outer Edge lines up off a mark below the level at which he last landed a race — a fair ask — with first-time cheekpieces adding fresh interest; he handles this trip on a sound surface and the trainer is in good form.

runners_data.name: Beelzebub
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's string is in form at 11/52 over 14 days and this horse ran to winning effect just seven days ago on Good ground over 6f — the freshness is an asset, though as a true hold-up type it must navigate heavy traffic from the rear, which this shape rarely rewards cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from landing a handicap at Windsor just seven days ago off the same mark he carries today, Beelzebub makes a quick reappearance with no penalty to carry; our top-rated runner who acts on this trip and going, he is the clear one to beat here.

runners_data.name: In Denial
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old hold-up performer whose recent form string of 74630 gives little confidence; Billy Loughnane rides, but with only two similar-going efforts from seven and no win at this level, the profile is unexciting and the race shape does not flatter late-closers here.
runners_data.comment: Capable of finding the frame when at her best, In Denial handles this trip and ground and lines up from draw 2; her Lingfield effort 34 days ago was well below par, and her form has been variable, but she remains a potential factor on her better days.

runners_data.name: Tickettothestars
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record with nine efforts in similar conditions and a win, two placings, and an eye-catching recent second over 6f on Good; Darragh Keenan is a capable claimer and this runner's hold-up profile, while naturally rear-facing, is the most exposed and form-backed of the closers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race by a length at Nottingham earlier this season off a mark 4lb below today's, Tickettothestars was well beaten last time at what appeared a challenging level; back on a mark she should handle and suited by the trip, she has claims despite the 1lb rise.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 3-year-old showed ability when third last time on Good over 6f, but a hold-up style that is being mapped forward by default does not sit naturally in a shape dominated by one front-runner; Luke Morris will need an early tactical decision, and limited similar-going experience (one from four) is a restraint.
runners_data.comment: Slow away at Brighton 20 days ago yet still ran to his level, beaten 2¼ lengths off this exact mark; shows promise in handicap company and should handle 5-6f on good ground, though yet to score and ranked fifth on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: The only genuine pace-setter in the race, giving David Egan full control of the tempo; Adrian Wintle's yard is active at 5/14 over 14 days, the mare handles Good ground and has run placed over this course-and-distance configuration, though an OR of 45 relative to the field and a style-fit caveat mean she is vulnerable if the closers arrive in a pack.
runners_data.comment: A below-par stable debut at Bath 24 days ago leaves questions unanswered, though she handles 6f on a sound surface and brings some Irish form as background; last on our figures, she is hard to fancy with confidence here.

races.paceDynamic: Jackie Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pace pressure in a six-runner field on Good ground at Ffos Las, she can control this entirely on her own terms — dictating tempo from the outset and manufacturing a rail-hugging, energy-efficient lead. The remainder of the field — Outer Edge, Beelzebub, Lieutenant Sir, In Denial, and Tickettothestars — are all genuine hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace Jackie Brown sets is unlikely to be aggressive enough to fry the field; she can simply roll along and control the fractions. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — Outer Edge, Beelzebub, and Lieutenant Sir are all true hold-up operators who will be competing for ground from the back, likely shuffled wider or forced into an unnatural position. A controlled, front-runner-led race on flat Ffos Las turf in Good conditions historically rewards the horse who travels sweetly close to the pace and finishes with a sustained burst rather than a pure sprint-finish late-closer; the tactical verdict is clear — prominent racers and those who can track Jackie Brown efficiently are most favoured, while true hold-up types face a compromised scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackie Brown Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown leads unchallenged and sets a fair-to-steady tempo throughout the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Jackie Brown leads unchallenged and sets a fair-to-steady tempo throughout the six furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown's pace is slow enough that several hold-up runners arrive in a late rush with the rail position failing to insulate the leader.
scenarios.body: If Jackie Brown's pace is slow enough that several hold-up runners arrive in a late rush with the rail position failing to insulate the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tracking Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-to-midfield tracker travels smoothly just off Jackie Brown and times a challenge perfectly entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If a prominent-to-midfield tracker travels smoothly just off Jackie Brown and times a challenge perfectly entering the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely, causing bunching, interference, or erratic fractions that scramble all form lines.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely, causing bunching, interference, or erratic fractions that scramble all form lines.

watchPoints.text: Jackie Brown's front-running position is entirely uncontested — watch whether David Egan elects to steal a march or conserve energy, as the tempo choice made at the start will define the entire race shape.

Beelzebub's very short turnaround of seven days means fitness is likely but race-fitness against fresher rivals could be tested in the final furlong — watch for signs of fatigue after a competitive recent effort.

Tickettothestars, In Denial, Lieutenant Sir, Outer Edge, and Beelzebub are all hold-up types converging on the same narrow patch of track in the final two furlongs — watch for significant crowding, traffic issues, and potential interference as they all angle for the same gaps simultaneously.

Lieutenant Sir dropped markedly in trip from his last two starts on Standard ground to 6f on Good today — watch whether he travels kindly enough in the early stages to be a factor, or whether the change in conditions and trip sees him outpaced.

races.name: Diplomat Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Rogue Enforcer
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse for Archie Watson and Luke Morris, but his similar-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 4 runs on Good gives little confidence he can generate the momentum from the rear in a race unlikely to be run at a searching enough pace to reel in the leader.
runners_data.comment: Has struggled to find his best this season, with his mark of 87 looking a stiff ask after being beaten well adrift at Epsom on his latest outing; first-time blinkers could sharpen him up and he handles the trip on a sound surface, but ranks bottom of the field on our figures.

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who has placed twice from 8 similar-going starts and is lightly raced for Christopher Mason; racing off a 42-day break is a minor query, but the unchallenged lead over 5f here is a significant positional asset and her STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant — this is precisely her role and she gets it by default in this small field.
runners_data.comment: Solid earlier in the season with a pair of placed efforts, this gelding steps out without headgear 42 days on from a below-par Windsor run; our top-rated runner on a trip and going he handles, with the yard in fine form currently.

runners_data.name: El Bufalo
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over on this Thomas Faulkner-trained five-year-old, who sports a tongue tie for the first time and is fresh at 16 days since last run; his hold-up style produced two runner-up efforts from soft-ground starts but his similar-going record on Good is 0 wins and 0 places from 3 runs, making the surface a quiet concern.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer over today's trip on a sound surface, El Bufalo is 16 days on from a tough run in a higher grade at York; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are an interesting addition, though the mark of 78 may be at the ceiling of his current range.

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old is in red-hot trainer form (7 from 27 over 14 days) and Billy Loughnane is a significant booking; naturally prominent, Zighy has 3 places from 4 similar-going runs and his experience of racing on Standard and Good going suggests he can travel comfortably just off the pace — he is the horse most likely to occupy the crucial tracking position behind All Ways Glamorous.
runners_data.comment: A progressive filly with two wins in her last five outings, Zighy ran to her mark last time but went for home too early and was caught close to the line; back at the minimum trip with a trainer in fine form, she has solid claims on her best.

runners_data.name: Comic Strip
runners_data.note: This Simon & Ed Crisford three-year-old is a genuine prominent racer by nature — Sean Bowen takes over from the saddle — but with Zighy also looking to press from close up, Comic Strip is the one more likely to be shuffled back from his preferred slot; his single similar-going run produced 0 wins and 0 places, and his STYLE_FIT discount reflects that racing further back than ideal is a real possibility here.
runners_data.comment: Back to the minimum trip after the extra yardage found him out at Windsor 37 days ago, Comic Strip acts on quick surfaces and goes from stall 1; rated third on our figures, he has strong claims if the drop in distance sharpens him up.

races.paceDynamic: All Ways Glamorous is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger willing to press for the lead, she is set to control proceedings from the outset at a sustainable, self-selected gallop over this 5f at Ffos Las. Zighy and Comic Strip are both naturally prominent types who will look to track close, though Comic Strip has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply not enough room at the head of affairs for all three pace-inclined horses — Zighy, with Billy Loughnane aboard for a trainer in sharp 7/27 form, is the likelier of the two to secure the position behind All Ways Glamorous. Rogue Enforcer and El Bufalo will come from off the pace, but on a flat 5f course with a controlled tempo, the gap between them and the leader may never compress enough for a decisive late challenge. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the controlled pace and produce a sustained effort in the final furlong, rather than true hold-up horses attempting to make up ground in a race run without genuine pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If All Ways Glamorous leads undisturbed and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits her rhythm.
scenarios.body: If All Ways Glamorous leads undisturbed and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that suits her rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If All Ways Glamorous sets a fractionally too-generous pace and Zighy or Comic Strip tracks efficiently before asserting in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If All Ways Glamorous sets a fractionally too-generous pace and Zighy or Comic Strip tracks efficiently before asserting in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to compromise All Ways Glamorous and the held-up runners find the gap they need late.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to compromise All Ways Glamorous and the held-up runners find the gap they need late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If All Ways Glamorous is challenged hard early by multiple prominent types and the race dissolves into a scramble in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: If All Ways Glamorous is challenged hard early by multiple prominent types and the race dissolves into a scramble in the final 2f.

watchPoints.text: All Ways Glamorous has the unchallenged lead — if she hits the front and is never pressured, watch whether any rival can close within a length by the 2f marker, as failure to do so by that point makes her very hard to catch.

Zighy's positioning in the opening furlong is critical — if Billy Loughnane secures the slot directly behind All Ways Glamorous, Zighy becomes the dominant danger; if Comic Strip pushes him wider or back, the shape changes materially.

Comic Strip's actual early behaviour at the stalls and in the first furlong will reveal whether he can find a prominent position despite the redistribution — Sean Bowen's tactical awareness will be key in a five-runner field with limited room to manoeuvre.

El Bufalo's tongue tie is a first-time application — watch the paddock and early running for any sign of improved relaxation, as a calmer demeanour behind the pace would be a positive sign for his late effort.

All Ways Glamorous has had 42 days off — monitor how she moves to post and whether she shows her usual forward intent in the stalls, as any sluggishness at the break could hand Zighy the lead and transform the shape entirely.

races.name: Dress For The Occasions Handicap

runners_data.name: Mayberry Moon
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 293-day absence for Michael Dods and David Egan, this two-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer who won over 7f on soft; the long layoff is the overriding concern and she will need everything to go right from the back on good ground.|
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 293-day absence and was excessively keen before the race at Carlisle last time, finishing down the field; effective over 7f with some cut in the ground, though the current mark looks a tough ask and a show of real improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: William Knight's three-year-old has been placed twice in five runs this season and arrives on a tight 15-day turnaround wearing headgear; runs prominently and should secure a forward position naturally, making this tactical draw the most straightforward in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Narrowly denied at Doncaster last time, beaten just a head off a mark 3lb lower, having been conceded a first-run advantage; on the upgrade in handicaps and effective at 7f-1m on good to soft and good to firm, he rates the one to beat with first-time cheekpieces added here.

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: The sole certified front-runner, Archie Watson's three-year-old has tactical speed and a win at 7f on Tapeta; going profile shows all recorded starts on artificial surfaces so good turf is a surface shift worth noting, but the uncontested lead is a sizeable structural advantage.|
runners_data.comment: Won by 4l at Kempton two starts ago off a mark 9lb lower, but went too soon over a longer trip last time and failed to see it out; the drop back in distance here is helpful, though the mark is unchanged and the trainer is out of form.

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's three-year-old has genuinely placed on good ground and was second over today's trip, but is a natural hold-up horse pushed forward on the map because the field is saturated with closers — do not expect Billy Loughnane to send this one forward; the style-fit discount is real.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Windsor last time, beaten just a length off this exact mark with a willing attitude; effective at 7f-1m and a genuine danger if she replicates that effort here, though inconsistency through her short career and a first-time tongue-tie both add an element of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Strong Voice
runners_data.note: Lightly raced for James Horton and returning from 79 days off, this hold-up type has placed on similar going at 7f; sits in midfield on the map only because the rear is overcrowded with closers, and its true style means it relies on pace that this uncontested leader is unlikely to supply.|
runners_data.comment: Failed to see out 1m at Yarmouth most recently but had shown good form at 7f on the all-weather prior; returning after a 79-day break on handicap debut, a rebound is needed but the earlier ability gives cause for hope if this shorter trip suits.

runners_data.name: Twilight Glow
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old wears a visor and has been placed over 7f at Sandown, but its entire recent profile is that of a back-of-the-field runner with no wins from eight starts; shunted forward on the map by redistribution, this horse will likely race towards the rear in reality.|
runners_data.comment: Pressed along too keenly when stepped up in trip at Windsor last time and may not have stayed, beaten 4l off a mark 3lb higher than today's; most effective over 6f with cut in the ground and a first-time visor could help, though still needing more to get fully involved.

runners_data.name: Victory Sound
runners_data.note: Mark Usher's four-year-old has the lowest OR in the field at 51 and a single win from fourteen starts, returning on 28 days; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield purely by redistribution, its best recent form came on Tapeta at Sandown rather than turf, adding a surface question to the style disadvantage.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Lingfield last time, beaten just 1¼l off a mark only 1lb higher than today's — he has been running consistently to his level of late and handles 7-8f on good ground and AW; with first-time cheekpieces added, he rates a danger from a workable mark.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press them hard from the outset, Luke Morris should be able to dictate a measured, controlled tempo over the 7½ furlongs at Ffos Las. The absence of genuine pace pressure means the fractions are likely to be honest but not punishing, leaving Quick Quasar with energy in reserve entering the final two furlongs. The field behind is dominated by hold-up horses — Flyta, Twilight Glow, Strong Voice, Victory Sound, and to a degree Mayberry Moon and Norfolk Blue — meaning closers will need to make sustained ground on a potentially front-running gallop that is never truly stressed. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce, or Quick Quasar itself if it controls the tempo uncontested; true hold-up horses are disadvantaged because the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to set them alight from the back. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle naturally at the rear, with Flyta, Twilight Glow, Strong Voice, and Victory Sound all pushed forward on the map — Quick Quasar and Norfolk Blue are most likely to actually secure their forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quasar Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar leads from flag to finish at a controlled pace and no rival has the will or speed to press early.
scenarios.body: If Quick Quasar leads from flag to finish at a controlled pace and no rival has the will or speed to press early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or mid-division horse tracks Quick Quasar closely and overpowers it inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a prominent or mid-division horse tracks Quick Quasar closely and overpowers it inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up horse finds clear late running.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true hold-up horse finds clear late running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar overcooks the fractions or suffers interference, scrambling the entire race shape.
scenarios.body: If Quick Quasar overcooks the fractions or suffers interference, scrambling the entire race shape.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar (Luke Morris) will attempt to lead from stall position — watch the first furlong to see if anything challenges for the front; if the leader gets a soft lead unchallenged the outcome is likely to be settled well before the final furlong.

Norfolk Blue (Taylor Fisher) is the most naturally placed horse to track Quick Quasar and represents the main structural threat — watch whether Fisher commits early to sit second, as any hesitation from midfield makes the task harder.

Flyta (Billy Loughnane) is flagged as a true hold-up type despite a midfield map position — if Loughnane rides conservatively to the rear as expected, discount any expectation of a forward move and watch whether it finds clear passage late.

Mayberry Moon (David Egan) is a 293-day returner; watch the market move at the off for trainer confidence signals, as a forward move in the ring would be the strongest indicator that the stable is happy with her condition after such a long break.

The going is uniformly Good across all distances today at Ffos Las — no hidden bias from one race to the next — but watch the rail position in the straight as runners tend to fan wide; any horse drawing a wide berth early could lose ground if the early pace is steady.

races.name: Preventapest Handicap

runners_data.name: Grey Soul
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with two wins over this exact trip, most recently on standard ground, giving him solid distance-and-surface credentials; Jason Watson times his challenges well but a steady pace is his enemy, and the 25-day break appears straightforward given he's clearly a fit horse in form.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap over this course and distance last time by half a length, performing at his best in the retained cheekpieces off a mark 3lb lower; effective at 7f-1m on good to soft, a modest step up in the weights looks very manageable.

runners_data.name: Bold Impact
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan's mount is the natural prominent rival to Orchard and has the best profile to press through the race — his good-ground form (placed in similar conditions) and consistent placing record make him the archetype winner in the dominant scenario, though his form string shows occasional disappointments.
runners_data.comment: Finished with purpose at Chepstow last time, beaten 3¼l off this exact mark; effective at 6-8f on soft and good to firm and with his trainer in form, he looks on a fair mark stepping back up to 1m and is a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Orchard
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's consistent sort carries a STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 suggesting he is not fully in role here, but as the one confirmed front-runner on good ground he does shape as the pace architect — his trainer's 14-day record of 0/11 is a mild negative, though the horse's ability to lead and control is the key race-shape factor.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form at this course and distance last time, beaten just a length off this exact mark despite not getting the clearest of runs; best at 1m on soft or AW ground and has a clear chance if he builds on that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Pulsar Star
runners_data.note: David Egan rides a horse who has placed on good ground over 8f twice in his history and carries a hurting plate, making him plausible in any scenario where the pace generates a true test; his 15-day turnaround is notably quick, but his trainer fired in a winner inside the 14-day window and he wears a hood, suggesting he is primed.
runners_data.comment: Below par at Doncaster last time, beaten 6l, and ranked fifth on our figures; effective at 7-8f on good and AW but winless in his last five starts, and first-time cheekpieces face a stiff task reversing a run of disappointing performances.

runners_data.name: Port Erin
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two wins on good ground over this trip, Billy Loughnane's positive style makes him the likeliest of the redistributed prominent-types to actually secure a forward berth — his recent form has been poor (0, 8, 11 in last three) and the style-fit discount (0.94) is real, but he should not be ignored if getting cover early.
runners_data.comment: Below his earlier level at Goodwood last time, beaten 8¼l, though he has shown he can perform over 8f on a sound surface; the mark may still be workable if he can recapture his better form, with this shorter, easier company his best chance.

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield map position by the redistribution logic; his form screams stamina limitations over 8f on standard ground (12th, 8th, 10th in last three on that trip), he fades in finishes by flag, and the 49-day break adds uncertainty — Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim helps carry the low weight but the evidence against is substantial.
runners_data.comment: Struggled badly at Wolverhampton most recently and ranks bottom on our figures; the return to turf is a genuine plus for a horse better suited to a sound surface, and first-time cheekpieces add a new angle, but he has been without a win in his last six starts and needs considerably more.

races.paceDynamic: Orchard is the one confirmed front runner here and, with only Bold Impact likely to press from a prominent position, the pace on good ground over a mile at Ffos Las should be measured and sustainable rather than frantic. Orchard will lead from the gates, establish a controlled tempo through the early stages, and the race is unlikely to be truly run — creating a premium on tactical position rather than raw finishing power. This shape favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and produce their effort from the two-furlong pole, making Bold Impact the most natural beneficiary profile; deep closers will face a stern test if the pace is genuinely moderate. Port Erin and Port Louis are both natural prominent-to-hold-up types who cannot all occupy their preferred positions in this small field — Port Erin is most likely to wrestle a forward berth given Billy Loughnane's positive riding style, while Port Louis is likely to find itself racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Orchard Controls; Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Orchard dictates a steady pace unchallenged and the closers cannot generate sufficient momentum from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: If Orchard dictates a steady pace unchallenged and the closers cannot generate sufficient momentum from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong enough, or the field fans wide turning in, creating genuine daylight for the closers.
scenarios.body: If the pace is deceptively strong enough, or the field fans wide turning in, creating genuine daylight for the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Port Erin Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If Loughnane rides Port Erin positively to secure a forward pitch and the pace compresses the field to suit a prominent finisher.
scenarios.body: If Loughnane rides Port Erin positively to secure a forward pitch and the pace compresses the field to suit a prominent finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses refuse to settle and the early tempo is higher than Orchard's profile suggests, causing a messy finish.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses refuse to settle and the early tempo is higher than Orchard's profile suggests, causing a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Orchard's early lead is critical — if Bold Impact or Port Erin pressures him from the gates, the pace quickens and the entire race shape shifts away from a controlled lead scenario.
Port Louis has a 49-day absence combined with a pattern of fading in finishes and poor recent form over the trip — any drift in the market late should be noted as an indicator of trainer confidence.

Grey Soul's hold-up style is entirely at the mercy of Orchard's tempo — if the gallop is genuinely slow, Grey Soul may find himself with too much ground to make up off a home turn where Ffos Las doesn't provide a long straight.

Pulsar Star's 15-day return and hood application suggest connections see him as sharp and ready — watch his pre-race demeanour and whether Egan positions him closer than the hold-up tag implies in running.

Bold Impact's jockey Gina Mangan has limited opportunities in competitive handicaps — monitor whether she rides positively to lock out Port Erin from the prominent berth, as both cannot hold their preferred position simultaneously.

races.name: Plan A Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Le Morbihan
runners_data.comment: Fell well short of his debut level at Doncaster last time, beaten 19l, so a clear rebound is required; effective over 10f on good ground and with the trainer in form, he has the profile to bounce back — he just needs to show it here.

runners_data.name: Marquessofanglesey
runners_data.comment: Beaten by the narrowest of margins in a maiden at Wolverhampton last time, performing to his level over 9f on the all-weather; he sets the standard here if his form carries across to turf, though that switch is the key question.

runners_data.name: Round The Table
runners_data.comment: Showed considerable promise on debut at Newbury despite inexperience — beaten 4l but doing enough to catch the eye over today's trip and going; there looks to be more in the locker after that initial outing, and he rates a solid chance stepping into a less demanding contest.

runners_data.name: Parc Dosne
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to a useful 1m-10f performer, his debut at Lingfield on soft ground was modest — the conditions may not have suited — and today's better surface gives every chance of improvement; the connections have been successful in this contest before.

runners_data.name: Seraglio Point
runners_data.comment: Failed to see out the extended trip at Windsor last time, falling below his debut level in a novice; more at home over 8f on the all-weather and yet to score in his last two starts — a significant rebound is required here.

races.name: Dress For The Occasions Handicap

runners_data.name: Calypso Bloom
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly who has finished eighth in her last three starts and carries a worrying fade-in-finish flag; 80 days off the track for Thomas Faulkner's yard, which has a poor recent strike rate, makes it hard to be enthusiastic at 1m4f against this field.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy based on these figures — she failed to trouble the judge when fourth beaten 8l in a novice last time, and remains without a win in her last three starts; middle-distance breeding at least gives hope over 12f on her return from an 80-day break.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and therefore tactically pivotal; Bernard Llewellyn's filly has two wins at 12f on similar ground and Alexandra Egan's 7lb claim is a significant asset, though the STYLE_FIT flag — reflecting that she is racing out of her usual role in terms of class of challenge — tempers confidence she can last home.
runners_data.comment: Below par in his last two starts, beaten 8l last time off a mark only 1lb higher; he has won twice in his last six and handles this trip and going, but sits at the bottom of our rankings with plenty to prove even with first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Buck Barrow
runners_data.note: Won once at 12f on soft but has since finished 6th, 10th and 6th; his true nature is as a hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map by the congested field, so his actual racing position will be further back than shown — Adrian Wintle's yard is in good recent form (4/14 T14) but the good ground is a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to land a classified event at this course and distance by a neck last time, showing he handles any going over 10-12f; the return to handicap company asks more, though the recent course form is solid and first-time cheekpieces add interest.

runners_data.name: Captain Cairney
runners_data.note: The most interesting profile in the race: a three-year-old with a win and two placings at 10f on good/standard who steps up to 1m4f; Muir & Grassick's colt has proven he can race prominently and his recent second on good going gives him the most relevant similar-ground form in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ran to his level when a close second, beaten just half a length off this exact mark last time; effective at 8-10f on soft and AW, and has a clear chance if he carries that forward — a touch of keenness the main concern with first-time cheekpieces here.

runners_data.name: Home Secretary
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old ran only nine days ago and the stable's one run in 14 days metric suggests restrained use of the stable's horses; a genuine deep hold-up type pushed into the midfield diagram by sheer numbers — his sole similar-going run is his only positive, but his current form figures of 5th, 9th, 7th, 6th, 6th inspire little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Tried in cheekpieces at Doncaster last time but failed to see out the trip, beaten 6½l; bred for 8-10f and stepping up to 12f here is a further stamina test, while a run just nine days ago adds to the challenge for a horse yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ataturk
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish warning and has finished 7th, 10th and 8th in his three career starts, all on soft or good-to-soft; the step to 1m4f on genuinely good ground for Hughie Morrison is a fresh question, and his position in the race map understates how far back he will naturally race — his form gives little reason to expect improvement.
runners_data.comment: A big, strong colt from a middle-distance family who has yet to score in his last three starts, but the step up to 12f in handicap company could be the key change; his trainer is in fine form and there is scope for the real ability to surface over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Worlington
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old has placed twice at 8f on good ground and recorded a fourth at 12f on good most recently; tongue-tie fitted and Billy Loughnane is a strong booking — naturally a hold-up horse who will race further back than the midfield map suggests, but his good-ground placed form makes him one of the more interesting deep runners if Beaune's pace is anything other than slow.
runners_data.comment: Second twice in recent starts and runs off the same official mark here; he was never at ease last time but the track and conditions may not have suited, and a first-time tongue-tie gives a new angle — he has a fair chance of recapturing his earlier level if this combination clicks.

runners_data.name: Ibn Sirin
runners_data.note: Returning from 257 days off for Harry Charlton after three juvenile runs, the most promising of which was a fourth on good going at 8f; a big unknown stepping to 1m4f on return, will race at the back as a natural hold-up type well behind what the map shows, and Edward Greatrex's ride cannot compensate for the lack of recent competitive experience.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 257-day absence and since been gelded — a significant change for a big colt who was pulling far too hard in his last start; stepping into handicap company for the first time could help channel his energy and unlock a more measured effort, though a long layoff is a real test.

races.paceDynamic: Beaune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to stride to the front unchallenged and control a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground at Ffos Las. The remaining seven runners — Calypso Bloom, Buck Barrow, Captain Cairney, Home Secretary, Ataturk, Worlington and Ibn Sirin — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, meaning the field behind Beaune will be compressed into a pack with riders jostling for position rather than pressing the pace. This creates a single-file, controlled tempo scenario where the advantage lies with horses that can travel close enough to make one clean, sustained run from two furlongs out rather than those dependent on a scorching pace to produce a late burst. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of those, Captain Cairney and Worlington are best-placed to forge closer to the pace than their natural style suggests, while the deepest closers — Ibn Sirin, Ataturk and Home Secretary — will be furthest back and most dependent on a pace that simply may not materialise. This race shape firmly favours a prominent-to-mid racer who can track Beaune's uncontested lead and pick her off in the straight, not a pure closer waiting for a collapse that is unlikely to come.

watchPoints.text: Beaune's early position is the race-shaping factor — watch whether Alexandra Egan lets her stride to the front uncontested or whether any runner unexpectedly challenges for the lead before the first bend, as this will define the entire pace scenario.

Captain Cairney is stepping up in trip from 10f to 1m4f for the first time; if he travels smoothly in behind Beaune rather than dropping back into the pack, he becomes the most dangerous closer in the race given his good-ground placed form.

The cluster of true hold-up horses — Ibn Sirin, Home Secretary and Ataturk — will all be racing further off the pace than the map indicates; watch early to see if any rider forces one of them closer than expected, which would be the only way they enter the finish picture.

Worlington's tongue-tie and Billy Loughnane's booking for George Boughey deserves monitoring in the market; if supported, it suggests connections expect the headgear to produce a more forward-going display that would suit this controlled-pace shape better than a pure hold-up effort.
